body:
# Phase directive — «Console scaffold» (Epoch 6 — The fleet console, viola-0.2.0; the head entry `chk-eg54zv5h` at `dbb0c40e`)

**WHAT IS AN INPUT, AND WHAT IS NOT.** Of the folder this directive stands in, the ONLY files you read or snap are
this directive and the relay files a later send names. A fact the plan needs and this directive does not state is
ASKED of the overseer in the P3 block, never looked up.

**The operator is AWAY, reached only through the overseer**: raise NO question dialog for him. A fork that is his
is written to `{run_dir}/founder-forks.md` (the question, the options in order with each one's cost, the
recommendation marked); his answer comes later through the overseer. A boundary widening is never settled by a
delegate: it takes its most conservative arm, marked PROVISIONAL, when the entry builds whole on that arm — or the
phase stops there and says so in one line. A technical fork is answered by the overseer's relay at once. **This
phase makes NO live start, opens, moves, focuses or closes NO window on the operator's desktop, dispatches nothing
to the compositor, sends no key to a real terminal, runs no real `claude` in any form and no live arm of any
`scripts/r*.sh`, runs no mutation run, and reads nothing of the operator's real `~/.claude*` or `~/.viola` — a
`viola list` among them.** In your chat messages name a compiled screen literal, never print it. Every time you
write comes from `date -u`, read at the moment of writing.

## Facts, measured by the overseer at 2026-11-28T00:43:16Z — cite them as this directive's

- The tree at `dbb0c40e` = its upstream, ci#46087983798 green 7 of 7; two tracked bookkeeping paths dirty; 140
  records, all complete, 0 pending, 0 gated; coverage `verified 29/37 · deferred 2 · planned 6 · implemented 0 ·
  unclaimed 6` (the six: v2-12, v2-14, v2-15, v2-28, v2-30, v2-31; v2-12 is released to «The fleet on the
  founder's host»); `rec.py marks` rows 0 · entries 0.
- The entry's head as the route holds it: «Console scaffold — its surface section, quarter-screen layout and
  redraw-ban reconciliation; a keystroke test driver reading state, never the screen; its own diagnostics role».
  It carries `cry-h6vzhlce` (the chrono advisory RUSTSEC-2026-0543 re-read — the operator's, owed since the Epoch
  5 boundary and not yet answered) and `cry-boujwuyr` (the Epoch 5 boundary audit's M1 — `framing_turns` /
  `send_through` — and M3, the relied-row count from one source). Read them from the store. Epoch 6 then holds
  «Fleet console view», «Console actions», «The fleet on the founder's host» (BLOCKED-ON R4), «Fleet a11y
  verification», «Version done-check».
- This is the first entry that builds an interactive surface: the masters' web sections were cut to a stub in
  0.1.0 («deferred to 0.2.0, technology not chosen») and the 0.2.0 intent carries the console; the operator's
  standing directions are «headless agent verification first» (every layer agent-runnable, the fake agent and
  fixtures the contract, structured logs from every process) and «infra before features» (no crate without a real
  consumer and a test).
- The host is Viola's today: the neighbour project is at rest. A gate red with no failed assertion is still read
  against `python3 ~/dev/projects/additional/andromedaV3/andromeda-overseer/docs/tools/hostwatch.py read --from
  <UTC> --to <UTC>` first and never re-run for green; read `df -m /tmp` beside it.

## The directive

1. Scope is the route entry and its two carries as they stand at `dbb0c40e` — a SCAFFOLD: the surface's section
   in the masters, its layout, the redraw-ban reconciliation, the test driver and the diagnostics role. No view of
   the fleet and no action belongs here («Fleet console view» and «Console actions» own them); say at P1, clause
   by clause of the head, what this entry builds and what it leaves to those two, and which of the six unclaimed
   capabilities — if any — a scaffold can honestly claim. A capability whose acceptance needs the view or a live
   terminal is NOT claimed here.
2. **Measurements first, at P3, each a number or a closed word from the code, a test, the masters or a
   dependency's own documentation:** what the tree already holds for a terminal surface (the pty pump, the screen
   reader, the terminal-size handling) and what a console needs that it lacks; every row of the masters that the
   console's redraw touches — the «redraw ban» rows by name, with their text — and what «reconciliation» must
   settle; the candidate ways to draw and to read keys with their cost in new dependencies (count, licences
   against `deny.toml`'s permissive list, MSRV, advisories); how a keystroke driver can read STATE and never the
   screen, and what the fake side of it is; what «its own diagnostics role» means against the existing roles
   (`run` / `hook` / `mcp` / `ui`) and the `logs` command.
3. **Forks, each with its options priced and marked his or technical.** His, at the least: any NEW dependency
   that draws or reads a terminal (a technology choice the 0.1.0 stub left open); any row of the redraw ban that
   the console must narrow or except (a boundary widening: its conservative arm is an exception NAMED for the
   console's own surface, the rule never generalised); what the console is started by (a new verb, a flag) and
   its name; the chrono advisory's re-read (`cry-h6vzhlce`: measure FIRST whether a safe upgrade of `chrono`
   exists and how cargo-deny treats an ignored id once one does; then his options — upgrade and drop the ignore,
   keep the ignore one more epoch — each priced). Say plainly whether one implement window holds the scaffold
   with `cry-boujwuyr`'s two items, and if not, the split you would make — a split is his.
4. Read the playbook's escalate rows BEFORE the P3 block is written. Search ALL seven masters by the counted
   literals a row or a test pins (the roles' list and its count, the verbs' list, the redraw rows, the dependency
   allowlist, the terminal-size rows) and by «never», «only»; name every reached row with the read-not-reached
   beside it.
5. **At P3's END, before P4:** ONE block in `founder-forks.md` — your window, the measurements, every reached
   row, each fork of his with the arm taken PROVISIONAL meanwhile, and whether the entry builds whole on those
   arms. If it does, go on to P4 without waiting; if a fork of his has no conservative arm that builds (a
   technology choice is likely one), STOP there and say so in one line — the overseer brings him the block.
6. A step that asserts what existing code does cites the symbol and line it read. Every `gate.py control` has an
   id of 1–16 characters, its `--timeout S`, and an entry filtered to its guard's own cases. Every filter term
   SELECTS at least one test under its layer flag once its step is built. An expect atom must be able to fail —
   an entry that reads a record must read red on an empty one; a word that may honestly read two ways is a
   READING (`expect = []`). The boot path: the plan holds the harness smoke trio as operator entries if a start
   path changes. Any test that drives the console runs under a test-owned home and its own pseudo-terminal,
   never the session's terminal, and takes a bound under the 20 s lint.
7. A guard's or the permission classifier's refusal is never routed around: stop and tell the overseer. Call NO
   scheduled-wake or timer tool. End every process you start; remove no scratch clone by a recursive delete —
   name it on the card. Scripted edits are followed by the formatter. Leaves hold no figure the code states.
8. Run the phase exactly as the letters say, read as they stand. On the P5 card, in one block, verbatim where a
   tool printed it: the union's per-master lines and the `rows-union` line; whether EVERY cited row is in the
   union or its standing list; planlint's own lines whole; the claim's lines for any capability claimed; every
   `[RETYPED]` line and re-spawn; every non-zero exit, refusal, `UNPARSED` / `INDETERMINATE` / `NOT DERIVED`
   line; every place a letter was wrong or silent.

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-11-28-console-scaffold · **Version:** viola-0.2.0
- **Taken up at:** `dbb0c40e` (CI ci#46087983798 green 7/7, 883 s wall)

- **His forks:** `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-28T00-46-52Z-phase/founder-forks.md` (P3 block). Every arm below marked
  PROVISIONAL is the conservative arm of a fork of his, taken under the overseer's directive (inputs#I1 items 3 and 5)
  until his own word; the plan builds whole on those arms.

Stand up the terminal fleet console's scaffold — the one view beyond `viola list` (architecture ·
decision/terminal-fleet-console) — as a verb that owns its terminal, draws one frame that stays whole at the floor size
and says so below it, reads its own keys, quits cleanly, and logs every state change under a console role of its own.
No fleet row, no lineage and no verb action is drawn or reached here: those are «Fleet console view» (v2-14) and
«Console actions» (v2-15, v2-31's console leg). The scaffold is what they build on: a keystroke driver that reads the
console's STATE (its codes-only role-file lines and its exit), never the screen (test-plan ·
decision/tui-verdicts-from-records), proves each behaviour over a test-owned home and the test's own pseudo-terminal.

Technology (F1, PROVISIONAL): no new dependency. The frame writer and the key decoder are hand-written in the root bin,
over the PTY seam's existing raw mode and size read (`viola_pty::HostTerminal`, `viola_pty::host_size`), as the SGR
module already is (design-system · decision/hand-written-sgr-module, «adds no dependency»; architecture ·
decision/libc-only-os-binding). Start (F3, PROVISIONAL): a new verb `viola console`, in the `board:` help row. The
redraw / interactive-input rows the console reaches (F2) each take an exception NAMED for the console's own surface —
written at the wrap as his, never generalised. Floor size (Q1, PROVISIONAL): 80×24, `Size::DEFAULT`.

The chunk also carries the Epoch 5 boundary's two code items (`cry-boujwuyr`): M1, `framing_turns`' five hand-written
per-paste blocks become one step function; M3, the relied-row count comes from `LedgerRow::ALL` through one constant
with one pin. And `cry-h6vzhlce`'s re-read is done and recorded: no safe chrono upgrade exists (research, 2026-11-28),
the ignore stands one more epoch on his word (F4, PROVISIONAL) with `deny.toml` unchanged.

1. **The console role** — `crates/viola-core/src/obs.rs`: `ObsProcess::Console`, `as_str` → `console`, `ALL` grows to
   five; the test at line 195-196 pins the five words in order. Two new closed `ObsEvent` values, `console-frame`
   (fields: `cols`, `rows`, `fits` — numbers and a boolean) and `console-key` (field: `key`, one of the closed words
   `quit` · `interrupt` · `unbound`), each in `ObsEvent`'s `as_str` and its doc's closed list. Keeps obs S1, S2.

3. **The role file** — `src/obs.rs` `role_file_name`: `(ObsProcess::Console, _)` → `console.ndjson`, home-level, no
   instance (as `mcp`); its rstest table at line 404 gains the case. `open_role_file`'s strict check stands in front of
   it unchanged (architecture · decision/diagnostics-open-checks-modes).

4. **The role from argv** — `src/main.rs`: `Role::Console`; `role_of` (line 91) maps the first word `console` to it;
   `exit_code` (line 137) treats it as a silent role: on a dispatch error or a caught panic it prints nothing (the
   terminal is the frame's) and exits 1 (architecture · decision/silent-roles-at-internal-error-catch, which the wrap
   extends). Its rstest table (line 350) gains `console` and `--home x console` cases.

5. **The verb** — `src/cmd/mod.rs`: `Command::Console` (no args, the global `--home` only), its doc line «Show the
   terminal fleet console in this terminal (the human's)», dispatched to `src/cmd/console.rs`; `HELP_TEMPLATE`'s
   `board:` row becomes `board:    list, focus, console`. Keeps layouts S1 (its `--help` usage and `--home`), design S3
   (a flat verb name).

6. **The start** — `src/cmd/console.rs`, in order: resolve the home as every verb does; refuse with exit 1 when stdin or
   stdout is not a terminal — `unable: viola console needs a terminal` / `hint: run viola console in a terminal window`
   — before any home read; run the strict-modes check of the home (`viola_state::strict::check_read`, as `viola list`'s
   board scan does) before any log opens — a refusal exits 1 with `unable: viola console could not use its home` /
   `hint: make the viola home readable by you alone, then run viola console again` and writes no line (architecture ·
   decision/refused-check-writes-no-line); then obs init under `ObsProcess::Console` with no instance; one
   `process-start`. Both refusals are fixed-message lines (design S2, layouts S2), each named in
   `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs` and in the exit-cause catalogue `tests/cross_exit_causes.rs`.

7. **The frame and keys** — `src/console/` (new module, declared from `src/main.rs`): `HostTerminal::enter` for raw
   mode; the alternate screen entered and the cursor hidden on start, both undone on every exit path (a guard whose
   drop writes the restore sequence and drops `HostTerminal`); a frame drawn whole from the top-left: a first line
   `viola console` and a last line `q quit`, plain ASCII, no colour (design S1); when the size is below 80×24 the frame
   is ONE line, `viola console needs 80x24; this terminal is <cols>x<rows>`, and nothing else. Every draw logs one
   `console-frame{cols, rows, fits}`. The size is read through `viola_pty::host_size` at start and polled every 100 ms
   (as the pump polls, `crates/viola-pty/src/pump.rs:553`); a changed size redraws and logs. Keys are read from stdin in
   reads of at most 64 bytes into a fixed buffer (a bounded reader: named in `tests/contract_bounded_readers.rs` if its
   census does not take the statement as bounded): `q` → `console-key{key:"quit"}`; byte 0x03 →
   `console-key{key:"interrupt"}`; both end the loop; any other read → one `console-key{key:"unbound"}` per read, never
   its bytes (architecture · decision/codes-only-role-logs). On the end: the restore, then
   `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:0}`, exit 0. Every write to the terminal goes through the human module's
   writer, never a print macro (the workspace lints). No board read, no channel frame, no compositor call.

8. **The keystroke driver** — `tests/tui_console.rs` (a root E2E binary, `[[test]]` in `Cargo.toml`, test-plan ·
   decision/e2e-layer-by-binary-prefix): each case makes its own test home under `target/e2e-home` (tests S1), spawns
   the built `viola --home <home> console` under portable-pty's outer PTY at a size it chooses, as
   `tests/tui_passthrough.rs` does, and waits on lines of `<home>/diagnostics/console.ndjson` and the child's exit,
   never on screen bytes and never by sleep (tests S2; obs S6); every wait inside the 12 s root `WITHIN` (architecture ·
   decision/root-waits-share-one-bound) and the case under the 20 s lint. Cases (named
   `<subject>_<condition>_<expected>`, tests S4):
   - `console_at_the_floor_logs_a_whole_frame_and_quits_on_q` — 80×24: `console-frame` `cols 80 rows 24 fits true`;
     `q`: `console-key quit`, `process-exit` 0, child exit 0.
   - `console_below_the_floor_logs_a_frame_that_does_not_fit` — 60×20: `fits false`.
   - `console_resized_logs_a_new_frame_at_the_new_size` — 100×30 then 70×20: a second `console-frame` `fits false`.
   - `console_logs_an_unbound_key_by_class_alone` — `x`: `console-key unbound`, and no line holds the byte `x` as a
     value (a literal oracle on the line's key set).
   - `console_on_interrupt_exits_zero` — 0x03: `console-key interrupt`, exit 0.
   - `console_restores_the_terminal_on_quit` — after `q` the outer PTY's child terminal reads its saved modes back: the
     driver reads the PTY's line-mode flag (`ICANON`) before the start, while the frame stands (off) and after the
     quit (on), through `libc::tcgetattr` on the master's fd (portable-pty 0.9.0 `MasterPty::as_raw_fd`, its
     `src/lib.rs:114`), as the seam's own `line_input_on` probe reads it (`crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs:348-352`) — not
     the screen.
   - `console_without_a_terminal_refuses_before_any_line` — piped stdio (`std::process::Command`): exit 1, stderr the
     two literal lines, no `diagnostics/` file made.
   - `console_with_a_widened_home_refuses_and_writes_no_line` — home 0770: exit 1, the two literal lines, no
     `console.ndjson`, the home's mode as found.
   Every emitted line is schema-checked by the existing conformance gate over the test homes (obs S3).
9. **The help pin** — `tests/cli_output_plain.rs`: the `board:` row literal reads `board:    list, focus, console`.

10. **M3, one source** — `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs`: `pub const RELIED_COUNT: usize = LedgerRow::ALL.len();`
   beside `relied()`; `test_cases_stamps.rs` lines 82, 205, 918, 1108 read `RELIED_COUNT`, and ONE case keeps the pin,
   `assert_eq!(RELIED_COUNT, 29)` (the deliberate move at a new row); `src/cmd/verify.rs` tests (833-908): every
   `step_line(n, 29, …)` total and every expected `"[n/29] …"` string take `RELIED_COUNT`, the expected strings staying
   literal but for the total (tests S3), and the doc line «twenty-nine rows» reads «the relied count». The summary's
   counting rule is untouched: `pass`, or `absent` on the browser-tools row alone (architecture history,
   2026-11-18-browser-tools-prompt-modal).

11. **M1, one step function** — `src/cmd/verify/typed/turns.rs`: the guard → count → `paste_text` → `wait_for` →
   `box_wait` sequence written five times in `framing_turns` (line 152) becomes one private function `paste_turn` taking
   the paste text and the answered-predicate, returning the settled rows (or the stop); `framing_turns` calls it for the
   long, tag and newline pastes, the echo, the context and the compact paste, each keeping its own latency field and its
   order; `framing_turns`' signature and its two callers (`runs.rs:23`, `runs.rs:88`) are unchanged. `send_through`
   (`src/run/send.rs:90`): read its guarded section and record in the report whether its guard and the wait share a
   step; no code change unless the read finds the same five-fold shape (it was measured not to: research).

12. **The chrono re-read recorded** — no code or `deny.toml` change: the report's carry line records the 2026-11-28 read
   (crates.io newest 0.4.45, RustSec `patched = []`) and his PROVISIONAL keep (F4).
- `src/cmd/console.rs` — the verb's start: terminal check, strict check, obs init, the loop's call, the exit
- `src/console/` — the frame, the floor rule, the key decoder, the restore guard
- `tests/tui_console.rs` — the keystroke driver over its own outer PTY and test home
- `crates/viola-core/src/obs.rs` — `ObsProcess::Console`, two `ObsEvent` values, the pinned test
- `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` — the process word and the two events
- `schemas/diag-detail.v1.json` — the process word
- `src/obs.rs` — the console role file name
- `src/main.rs` — `Role::Console`, `role_of`, `exit_code`, `mod console`
- `src/cmd/mod.rs` — `Command::Console`, the `board:` row
- `tests/cli_output_plain.rs` — the help pin
- `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs` — the two refusal writers named
- `tests/cross_exit_causes.rs` — the two exit-1 causes and hints
- `tests/contract_bounded_readers.rs` — the key reader, if its census does not read it as bounded
- `Cargo.toml` — the `[[test]]` entry for `tui_console`
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` — `RELIED_COUNT`
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger/test_cases_stamps.rs` — the literals to `RELIED_COUNT`, one pin

The block runs, in order: the formatter and the linter; the core crate's and the ledger crate's units; the root
binaries' units; the console binary whole and its two control entries (0 selected on the untouched tree); the help,
M3 and M1 counts; the advisory read; the host read; the harness's unit, integration and e2e layers; then the operator
pass.

**What is not run, and why:** no round, no live entry, no live start and no real `claude` (inputs#I1); no mutation run.
No new dependency moves under F1's PROVISIONAL arm, so `cargo deny check` stands as CI's `supply-chain` job, beside
the advisory read below that records the chrono re-read. **Boot path:** test-plan declares no boot-path list; by shape
`src/main.rs`'s `role_of` and `exit_code` are on every start's path, so the harness smoke trio stands below as operator
entries. Every console test starts under a test-owned home and its own PTY.

**The remove-the-guard controls** are implement's one-shot `gate.py control` runs, never entries, each on its filtered

body:
8. **The keystroke driver** — `tests/tui_console.rs` (a root E2E binary, `[[test]]` in `Cargo.toml`, test-plan ·
   decision/e2e-layer-by-binary-prefix): each case makes its own test home under `target/e2e-home` (tests S1), spawns
   the built `viola --home <home> console` under portable-pty's outer PTY at a size it chooses, as
   `tests/tui_passthrough.rs` does, and waits on lines of `<home>/diagnostics/console.ndjson` and the child's exit,
   never on screen bytes and never by sleep (tests S2; obs S6); every wait inside the 12 s root `WITHIN` (architecture ·
   decision/root-waits-share-one-bound) and the case under the 20 s lint. Cases (named
   `<subject>_<condition>_<expected>`, tests S4):
   - `console_at_the_floor_logs_a_whole_frame_and_quits_on_q` — 80×24: `console-frame` `cols 80 rows 24 fits true`;
     `q`: `console-key quit`, `process-exit` 0, child exit 0.
   - `console_below_the_floor_logs_a_frame_that_does_not_fit` — 60×20: `fits false`.
   - `console_resized_logs_a_new_frame_at_the_new_size` — 100×30 then 70×20: a second `console-frame` `fits false`.
   - `console_logs_an_unbound_key_by_class_alone` — `x`: `console-key unbound`, and no line holds the byte `x` as a
     value (a literal oracle on the line's key set).
   - `console_on_interrupt_exits_zero` — 0x03: `console-key interrupt`, exit 0.
   - `console_restores_the_terminal_on_quit` — after `q` the outer PTY's child terminal reads its saved modes back: the
     driver reads the PTY's line-mode flag (`ICANON`) before the start, while the frame stands (off) and after the
     quit (on), through `libc::tcgetattr` on the master's fd (portable-pty 0.9.0 `MasterPty::as_raw_fd`, its
     `src/lib.rs:114`; Linux routes a termios read on a pty master to its slave), as the seam's own `line_input_on`
     probe reads `ICANON` (`crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs:451-458`) — not the screen.
   - `console_without_a_terminal_refuses_before_any_line` — piped stdio (`std::process::Command`): exit 1, stderr the
     two literal lines, no `diagnostics/` file made.
   - `console_with_a_widened_home_refuses_and_writes_no_line` — home 0770: exit 1, the two literal lines, no
     `console.ndjson`, the home's mode as found.
   Every emitted line is schema-checked by the existing conformance gate over the test homes (obs S3).

title: I2-relay-console-forks.md.txt
body:
# Relay — the operator's answers to the forks of «Console scaffold» (chunk 2026-11-28-console-scaffold, phase run 2026-11-28T00-46-52Z-phase)

**The operator's OWN answers**, given by two question dialogs (read at 2026-11-28T07:20:23Z and 07:30:02Z), each
option shown as `founder-forks.md` priced it. Each is his word, not a delegate's: nothing of it rests PROVISIONAL.

- **F1 — «Без зависимостей (Recommended)»**: no new dependency; the hand-written frame writer and key decoder over
  `HostTerminal` and `host_size`.
- **F2 — «Именное исключение (Recommended)»**: an exception NAMED for the console's own surface on each of the
  four reached rows (a11y-plan `decision/static-linear-output`, `decision/cli-not-keyboard-interactive`,
  `decision/cli-no-interactive-input`; obs-plan `absence/interactive-terminal-interface`), the rule never
  generalised. He was told it is a boundary widening and the four rows by name.
- **F3 — «Просто viola»** — HIS OWN TEXT, none of the three options: **the console starts on BARE `viola`, no
  verb.** `viola console` is NOT his word, neither is `list --live`; no alias beside it (default none — an alias
  is his to ask for).
- **F4 — «Держать ignore (Recommended)»**: the chrono ignore stays to the Epoch 7 boundary.
- **F5 — «Один чанк (Recommended)»**: one chunk, M1 and M3 last.
- **Q1 — «80×24 (Recommended)»**: the frame's stays-whole floor is 80×24, his word.
Technical, the overseer's, as said: Q2 (M3 is the 21 literal sites; no second table), Q3 (the role's word
`console`).

## What F3 changes — a REVISION of the plan, measurements first (the arm was never measured)

1. **Read what bare `viola` does today**, each a closed word or number from the code and a test: its answer with no
   argument (help, a usage error, which stream), its exit code, the rows that pin it (`contract/viola-help/*`, any
   row or test pinning the no-argument answer), every bare call in the harness, `scripts/`, CI and the tests, and
   the non-terminal cases (stdin not a terminal; stdout not a terminal; both).
2. **The conservative settlement, the overseer's technical word:** on a NON-terminal (stdin or stdout not a
   terminal) bare `viola` keeps today's answer byte for byte — a pipe, a script, CI and every existing test read
   what they read now. Only bare `viola` with both stdin and stdout a terminal starts the console. `viola --help`
   and every verb are unchanged. If the measurement shows this cannot hold, or that it changes what he gets at
   his keyboard beyond «the console opens», STOP and say so with the measurement — that one question goes back to
   him.
3. **What moves in the plan:** no `Command::Console` verb and no `board:` help-row change (step 5, step 9, the
   acceptance's help line) unless the measurement says the help must name the bare start — say where the help
   tells a user the console exists; the role still reads from the start (`role_of`: the no-argument, both-terminal
   case → `console`); the keystroke driver starts bare `viola` under its own PTY; a new case pins the
   non-terminal answer unchanged. The F2 exceptions are named for «the terminal fleet console, bare `viola` on a
   terminal».
4. Search the masters again by the new literals (the no-argument answer, the help's first lines, the exit code of
   a usage error) and name every reached row with the read-not-reached beside it. A row the bare start reaches
   that F2's four do not is a NEW widening: its conservative arm is the same named exception, and it is named on
   the card as his to confirm.
5. Revise through the phase's own door, re-run the P5 checks, and stop at the card.

body:
- **His answers:** inputs#I2 (the operator's own, by two question dialogs, 2026-11-28T07:20:23Z and 07:30:02Z): F1 no
  dependency · F2 a named exception on each of the four reached rows · F3 «Просто viola», his own text — the console
  starts on bare `viola`, no verb, no alias · F4 the chrono ignore stays to the Epoch 7 boundary · F5 one chunk, M1 and
  M3 last · Q1 the floor 80×24. The overseer's technical answers (inputs#I2): Q2 M3 is the literal sites only, no second
  table · Q3 the role word `console`. His forks as priced: `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-28T00-46-52Z-phase/founder-forks.md`.

- **Revised at P5's review** (p5-card-1, the word «review»): F3's answer moved the start from a verb to bare `viola`;
  the bare-start settlement is the overseer's technical word (inputs#I2 §What F3 changes, item 2).

Stand up the terminal fleet console's scaffold — the one view beyond `viola list` (architecture ·
decision/terminal-fleet-console) — started by bare `viola` with stdin and stdout both a terminal. It owns that
terminal, draws one frame that stays whole at 80×24 and says so below it, reads its own keys, quits cleanly, and logs
every state change under a console role of its own. Off a terminal (stdin or stdout not one) bare `viola` keeps
today's answer byte for byte — the help text on stderr, stdout empty, exit 2 (measured, research §Revision 1) — so a
pipe, a script, CI and every existing test read what they read now; `viola --help` and every verb are unchanged. No
fleet row, no lineage and no verb action is drawn or reached here: those are «Fleet console view» (v2-14) and
«Console actions» (v2-15, v2-31's console leg). A keystroke driver reads the console's STATE (its codes-only role-file
lines and its exit), never the screen (test-plan · decision/tui-verdicts-from-records), over a test-owned home and the
test's own pseudo-terminal.

Technology (F1, his word): no new dependency. The frame writer and the key decoder are hand-written in the root bin,
over the PTY seam's existing raw mode and size read (`viola_pty::HostTerminal`, `viola_pty::host_size`), as the SGR
module already is (design-system · decision/hand-written-sgr-module, «adds no dependency»; architecture ·
decision/libc-only-os-binding). The redraw and interactive-input rows the console reaches (F2, his word, a boundary
widening) each take an exception NAMED for «the terminal fleet console, bare `viola` on a terminal» — written at the
wrap, never generalised. One more row the bare start reaches, `(obs-plan · decision/role-classified-before-clap)`, takes
the same named exception: a NEW widening, his to confirm (card). Floor (Q1, his word): 80×24, `Size::DEFAULT`.

The chunk also carries the Epoch 5 boundary's two code items (`cry-boujwuyr`): M1, `framing_turns`' five hand-written
per-paste blocks become one step function; M3, the relied-row count comes from `LedgerRow::ALL` through one constant
with one pin — the carry's «stamped-set table held once» met by that constant, no second table standing (Q2). And
`cry-h6vzhlce`'s re-read is done and recorded: no safe chrono upgrade exists (research, 2026-11-28), the ignore stands
to the Epoch 7 boundary on his word (F4) with `deny.toml` unchanged.

1. **The console role** — `crates/viola-core/src/obs.rs`: `ObsProcess::Console`, `as_str` → `console` (Q3), `ALL` grows
   to five; the test at line 195-196 pins the five words in order. Two new closed `ObsEvent` values, `console-frame`
   (fields: `cols`, `rows`, `fits` — numbers and a boolean) and `console-key` (field: `key`, one of the closed words
   `quit` · `interrupt` · `unbound`), each in `ObsEvent`'s `as_str` and its doc's closed list. Keeps obs S1, S2.

4. **The role from argv and the terminal** — `src/main.rs`: `Role::Console`; `role_of` (line 91) returns it only when
   the arguments hold no verb — none at all, or only the global `--home <dir>` / `--home=<dir>` — AND stdin and stdout
   are both a terminal (`std::io::IsTerminal` on both); with no verb off a terminal it returns `Role::Other` as today
   (line 120). Every other argument list keeps its role. `exit_code` (line 137) treats `Console` as a silent role: on a
   dispatch error or a caught panic it prints nothing (the terminal is the frame's) and exits 1 (architecture ·
   decision/silent-roles-at-internal-error-catch, which the wrap extends). Its rstest table (line 350) gains the
   no-verb cases, the terminal facts passed in (the decision a pure function of the args and two booleans, so the unit
   cases need no terminal).

5. **No verb: the console or today's answer** — `src/cmd/mod.rs`: `Cli`'s `command` (line 61) becomes optional; with
   no verb, both a terminal → `src/cmd/console.rs`; else today's answer, byte for byte: the rendered help text on
   stderr (the same bytes `viola --help` writes on stdout), nothing on stdout, exit 2 — what clap's missing-verb answer
   writes now. `HELP_TEMPLATE` (line 36), `viola --help`, `viola help` and every verb are unchanged; no `Console`
   variant and no alias (F3). The help does not name the console: its text is the non-terminal answer itself, which
   must not move (research §Revision 1). Keeps layouts S1 (no new verb owes a help row).

6. **The start** — `src/cmd/console.rs`, in order: resolve the home as every verb does (`--home`, else the default);
   run the strict-modes check of the home (`viola_state::strict::check_read`, as `viola list`'s board scan does,
   `crates/viola-state/src/board.rs:67`) before any log opens — a refusal exits 1 with
   `unable: viola could not use its home` / `hint: make the viola home readable by you alone, then run viola again`
   and writes no line (architecture · decision/refused-check-writes-no-line); then obs init under
   `ObsProcess::Console` with no instance; one `process-start`. The refusal is a fixed-message pair (design S2, layouts
   S2) named in `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs` and in the exit-cause catalogue `tests/cross_exit_causes.rs`. Its
   stderr is written before raw mode and the alternate screen, so it reads on the terminal as a verb's refusal does.

8. **The keystroke driver** — `tests/tui_console.rs` (a root E2E binary, `[[test]]` in `Cargo.toml`, test-plan ·
   decision/e2e-layer-by-binary-prefix): each case makes its own test home under `target/e2e-home` (tests S1), spawns
   the built `viola --home <home>` with no verb under portable-pty's outer PTY at a size it chooses, as
   `tests/tui_passthrough.rs` does, and waits on lines of `<home>/diagnostics/console.ndjson` and the child's exit,
   never on screen bytes and never by sleep (tests S2; obs S6); every wait inside the 12 s root `WITHIN` (architecture ·
   decision/root-waits-share-one-bound) and the case under the 20 s lint. Cases (named
   `<subject>_<condition>_<expected>`, tests S4):
   - `console_at_the_floor_logs_a_whole_frame_and_quits_on_q` — 80×24: `console-frame` `cols 80 rows 24 fits true`;
     `q`: `console-key quit`, `process-exit` 0, child exit 0.
   - `console_below_the_floor_logs_a_frame_that_does_not_fit` — 60×20: `fits false`.
   - `console_resized_logs_a_new_frame_at_the_new_size` — 100×30 then 70×20: a second `console-frame` `fits false`.
   - `console_logs_an_unbound_key_by_class_alone` — `x`: `console-key unbound`, and no line holds the byte `x` as a
     value (a literal oracle on the line's key set).
   - `console_on_interrupt_exits_zero` — 0x03: `console-key interrupt`, exit 0.
   - `console_restores_the_terminal_on_quit` — the driver reads the PTY's line-mode flag (`ICANON`) before the start,
     while the frame stands (off) and after the quit (on), through `libc::tcgetattr` on the master's fd (portable-pty
     0.9.0 `MasterPty::as_raw_fd`, its `src/lib.rs:114`; Linux routes a termios read on a pty master to its slave), as
     the seam's own `line_input_on` probe reads `ICANON` (`crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs:451-458`) — not the screen.
   - `bare_viola_off_a_terminal_answers_as_today` — three rstest cases, no stdio a terminal / stdin a terminal alone /
     stdout a terminal alone (the terminal side a PTY slave the test opens itself): stderr byte-equal to `viola --help`'s
     stdout, stdout empty, exit 2, and no `diagnostics/` made under the test home.
   - `console_with_a_widened_home_refuses_and_writes_no_line` — home 0770: exit 1, the two literal lines, no
     `console.ndjson`, the home's mode as found.
   Every emitted line is schema-checked by the existing conformance gate over the test homes (obs S3).
   `tests/run_cli.rs`'s `viola_without_a_verb_is_usage` (line 572) stands unchanged: it runs bare `viola` off a
   terminal and still reads exit 2.

9. **M3, one source** — `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs`: `pub const RELIED_COUNT: usize = LedgerRow::ALL.len();`
   beside `relied()`; `test_cases_stamps.rs` lines 82, 205, 918, 1108 read `RELIED_COUNT`, and ONE case keeps the pin,
   `assert_eq!(RELIED_COUNT, 29)` (the deliberate move at a new row); `src/cmd/verify.rs` tests (833-908): every
   `step_line(n, 29, …)` total and every expected `"[n/29] …"` string take `RELIED_COUNT`, the expected strings staying
   literal but for the total (tests S3), and the doc line «twenty-nine rows» reads «the relied count». No second table
   is touched: none stands (Q2). The summary's counting rule is untouched: `pass`, or `absent` on the browser-tools row
   alone (architecture history, 2026-11-18-browser-tools-prompt-modal).

10. **M1, one step function** — `src/cmd/verify/typed/turns.rs`: the guard → count → `paste_text` → `wait_for` →
   `box_wait` sequence written five times in `framing_turns` (line 152) becomes one private function `paste_turn` taking
   the paste text and the answered-predicate, returning the settled rows (or the stop); `framing_turns` calls it for the
   long, tag and newline pastes, the echo, the context and the compact paste, each keeping its own latency field and its
   order; `framing_turns`' signature and its two callers (`runs.rs:23`, `runs.rs:88`) are unchanged. `send_through`
   (`src/run/send.rs:90`): read its guarded section and record in the report whether its guard and the wait share a

11. **The chrono re-read recorded** — no code or `deny.toml` change: the report's carry line records the 2026-11-28 read
   (crates.io newest 0.4.45, RustSec `patched = []`) and his keep to the Epoch 7 boundary (F4, inputs#I2).

(v2-14) and «Console actions» (v2-15, v2-31's console leg). The scaffold is what they build on: a keystroke driver that
reads the console's STATE (its codes-only role-file lines and its exit), never the screen (test-plan ·
decision/tui-verdicts-from-records), proves each behaviour over a test-owned home and the test's own pseudo-terminal.

Technology (F1, his word): no new dependency. The frame writer and the key decoder are hand-written in the root bin,
over the PTY seam's existing raw mode and size read (`viola_pty::HostTerminal`, `viola_pty::host_size`), as the SGR
module already is (design-system · decision/hand-written-sgr-module, «adds no dependency»; architecture ·
decision/libc-only-os-binding). Start (F3, his word): the verb `viola console`, in the `board:` help row; bare `viola`
keeps today's answer (the help on stderr, exit 2 — research §Revision 1). The redraw / interactive-input rows the console
reaches (F2, his word, a boundary widening) each take an exception NAMED for «the terminal fleet console
(`viola console`), its own surface» — written at the wrap, never generalised. Floor (Q1, his word): 80×24,
`Size::DEFAULT`.

4. **The role from argv** — `src/main.rs`: `Role::Console`; `role_of` (line 91) maps the first word `console` to it;
   `exit_code` (line 137) treats it as a silent role: on a dispatch error or a caught panic it prints nothing (the
   terminal is the frame's) and exits 1 (architecture · decision/silent-roles-at-internal-error-catch, which the wrap
   extends). Its rstest table (line 350) gains `console` and `--home x console` cases. With no argument `role_of` still
   returns `Role::Other` (line 120) and `Cli`'s `command` stays required (`src/cmd/mod.rs:61`): bare `viola` keeps
   today's answer (F3, inputs#I3).

5. **The verb** — `src/cmd/mod.rs`: `Command::Console` (no args, the global `--home` only), its doc line «Show the
   terminal fleet console in this terminal (the human's)», dispatched to `src/cmd/console.rs`; `HELP_TEMPLATE`'s
   `board:` row becomes `board:    list, focus, console` (F3, his word). Keeps layouts S1 (its `--help` usage and
   `--home`), design S3 (a flat verb name). No alias.

6. **The start** — `src/cmd/console.rs`, in order: resolve the home as every verb does; refuse with exit 1 when stdin or
   stdout is not a terminal — `unable: viola console needs a terminal` / `hint: run viola console in a terminal window`
   — before any home read; run the strict-modes check of the home (`viola_state::strict::check_read`, as `viola list`'s
   board scan does, `crates/viola-state/src/board.rs:67`) before any log opens — a refusal exits 1 with
   `unable: viola console could not use its home` / `hint: make the viola home readable by you alone, then run viola
   console again` and writes no line (architecture · decision/refused-check-writes-no-line); then obs init under
   `ObsProcess::Console` with no instance; one `process-start`. Both refusals are fixed-message lines (design S2,
   layouts S2), each named in `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs` and in the exit-cause catalogue
   `tests/cross_exit_causes.rs`.

8. **The keystroke driver** — `tests/tui_console.rs` (a root E2E binary, `[[test]]` in `Cargo.toml`, test-plan ·
   decision/e2e-layer-by-binary-prefix): each case makes its own test home under `target/e2e-home` (tests S1), spawns
   the built `viola --home <home> console` under portable-pty's outer PTY at a size it chooses, as
   `tests/tui_passthrough.rs` does, and waits on lines of `<home>/diagnostics/console.ndjson` and the child's exit,
   never on screen bytes and never by sleep (tests S2; obs S6); every wait inside the 12 s root `WITHIN` (architecture ·
   decision/root-waits-share-one-bound) and the case under the 20 s lint. Cases (named
   `<subject>_<condition>_<expected>`, tests S4):
   - `console_at_the_floor_logs_a_whole_frame_and_quits_on_q` — 80×24: `console-frame` `cols 80 rows 24 fits true`;
     `q`: `console-key quit`, `process-exit` 0, child exit 0.
   - `console_below_the_floor_logs_a_frame_that_does_not_fit` — 60×20: `fits false`.
   - `console_resized_logs_a_new_frame_at_the_new_size` — 100×30 then 70×20: a second `console-frame` `fits false`.
   - `console_logs_an_unbound_key_by_class_alone` — `x`: `console-key unbound`, and no line holds the byte `x` as a
     value (a literal oracle on the line's key set).
   - `console_on_interrupt_exits_zero` — 0x03: `console-key interrupt`, exit 0.
   - `console_restores_the_terminal_on_quit` — the driver reads the PTY's line-mode flag (`ICANON`) before the start,
     while the frame stands (off) and after the quit (on), through `libc::tcgetattr` on the master's fd (portable-pty
     0.9.0 `MasterPty::as_raw_fd`, its `src/lib.rs:114`; Linux routes a termios read on a pty master to its slave), as
     the seam's own `line_input_on` probe reads `ICANON` (`crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs:451-458`) — not the screen.
   - `console_without_a_terminal_refuses_before_any_line` — piped stdio (`std::process::Command`): exit 1, stderr the
     two literal lines, no `diagnostics/` file made.
   - `console_with_a_widened_home_refuses_and_writes_no_line` — home 0770: exit 1, the two literal lines, no
     `console.ndjson`, the home's mode as found.
   Every emitted line is schema-checked by the existing conformance gate over the test homes (obs S3).
   `tests/run_cli.rs`'s `viola_without_a_verb_is_usage` (line 572) stands unchanged and keeps reading exit 2.
9. **The help pin** — `tests/cli_output_plain.rs`: the `board:` row literal reads `board:    list, focus, console`.

10. **M3, one source** — `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs`: `pub const RELIED_COUNT: usize = LedgerRow::ALL.len();`
   beside `relied()`; `test_cases_stamps.rs` lines 82, 205, 918, 1108 read `RELIED_COUNT`, and ONE case keeps the pin,
   `assert_eq!(RELIED_COUNT, 29)` (the deliberate move at a new row); `src/cmd/verify.rs` tests (833-908): every
   `step_line(n, 29, …)` total and every expected `"[n/29] …"` string take `RELIED_COUNT`, the expected strings staying
   literal but for the total (tests S3), and the doc line «twenty-nine rows» reads «the relied count». No second table
   is touched: none stands (Q2). The summary's counting rule is untouched: `pass`, or `absent` on the browser-tools row
   alone (architecture history, 2026-11-18-browser-tools-prompt-modal).

11. **M1, one step function** — `src/cmd/verify/typed/turns.rs`: the guard → count → `paste_text` → `wait_for` →
   `box_wait` sequence written five times in `framing_turns` (line 152) becomes one private function `paste_turn` taking
   the paste text and the answered-predicate, returning the settled rows (or the stop); `framing_turns` calls it for the
   long, tag and newline pastes, the echo, the context and the compact paste, each keeping its own latency field and its
   order; `framing_turns`' signature and its two callers (`runs.rs:23`, `runs.rs:88`) are unchanged. `send_through`
   (`src/run/send.rs:90`): read its guarded section and record in the report whether its guard and the wait share a
   step; no code change unless the read finds the same five-fold shape (it was measured not to: research).

12. **The chrono re-read recorded** — no code or `deny.toml` change: the report's carry line records the 2026-11-28 read
   (crates.io newest 0.4.45, RustSec `patched = []`) and his keep to the Epoch 7 boundary (F4, inputs#I2).
- `src/cmd/console.rs` — the verb's start: terminal check, strict check, obs init, the loop's call, the exit
- `tests/tui_console.rs` — the keystroke driver over its own outer PTY and test home
- `src/cmd/mod.rs` — `Command::Console`, the `board:` row
- `tests/cli_output_plain.rs` — the help pin
- `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs` — the two refusal writers named
- `tests/cross_exit_causes.rs` — the two exit-1 causes and hints

The block runs, in order: the formatter and the linter; the core crate's and the ledger crate's units; the root
binaries' units; the console binary whole and its two control entries (0 selected on the untouched tree); the help,
M3 and M1 counts; the advisory read; the host read; the harness's unit, integration and e2e layers; then the operator
pass.

**What is not run, and why:** no round, no live entry, no live start and no real `claude` (inputs#I1); no mutation run.
No new dependency moves (F1), so `cargo deny check` stands as CI's `supply-chain` job, beside the advisory read below
that records the chrono re-read. **Boot path:** test-plan declares no boot-path list; by shape `src/main.rs`'s
`role_of` and `exit_code` are on every start's path, so the harness smoke trio stands below as operator entries.
Every console test starts under a test-owned home and its own PTY.

**The remove-the-guard controls** are implement's one-shot `gate.py control` runs, never entries, each on its filtered
entry below, `--timeout 900` (a clone build of the root crate and one case). Each case fails on its own bounded wait
(12 s `WITHIN`), so a `timeout` reading would NOT read the guard as held.
| `restore` | `src/console/` restore guard | the guard's drop body (made empty) | `console_restores_the_terminal_on_quit` | `ctl-restore` |

   instance (as `mcp`); its rstest table at line 404 gains the case. `open_role_file`'s strict check stands in front of
   it unchanged (architecture · decision/diagnostics-open-checks-modes). `internal_error_exit_line` (line 233) writes
   the catch site's `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"internal-error"}` for `ObsProcess::Console` too
   (its gate at line 235 reads `Run | Cli` today), so a console failure leaves its role line beside the stderr line.

4. **The role at the catch site** — `src/main.rs`: no new `Role` variant and no change to `role_of`, `exit_code` or
   `prints_internal_error`: the first word `console` falls to `Role::Cli` (line 116), as every other verb does, so a
   console dispatch error or caught panic prints `error: internal error` once on stderr (`human::internal_error`,
   main.rs:69; the line at `src/human.rs:49`) and exits 1 (main.rs:142) — the existing contract for a cli-role verb
   (architecture · contract/cli-internal-error/output), unamended; (architecture ·
   decision/silent-roles-at-internal-error-catch) is not reached (inputs#I4). `role_of`'s rstest table (line 350) gains
   `console` and `--home x console`, each reading `Role::Cli`. With no argument `role_of` still returns `Role::Other`
   (line 120) and `Cli`'s `command` stays required (`src/cmd/mod.rs:61`): bare `viola` keeps today's answer (F3,
   inputs#I3). **The order, restore then print, by construction:** the console's restore guard is owned inside
   `console::run`'s own frame, so it drops — writing the restore sequence and dropping `HostTerminal` — when `run`
   returns its error or when a panic unwinds through it, both before `std::panic::catch_unwind` (main.rs:49) returns;
   the print sits after that return (main.rs:66-70). Step 7's two unit cases prove the guard's half of that order.

7. **The frame and keys** — `src/console/` (new module, declared from `src/main.rs`): `HostTerminal::enter` for raw
   mode; the alternate screen entered and the cursor hidden on start, both undone on every exit path (a guard whose
   drop writes the restore sequence and drops `HostTerminal`); a frame drawn whole from the top-left: a first line
   `viola console` and a last line `q quit`, plain ASCII, no colour (design S1); when the size is below 80×24 the frame
   is ONE line, `viola console needs 80x24; this terminal is <cols>x<rows>`, and nothing else. Every draw logs one
   `console-frame{cols, rows, fits}`. The size is read through `viola_pty::host_size` at start and polled every 100 ms
   (as the pump polls, `crates/viola-pty/src/pump.rs:553`); a changed size redraws and logs. Keys are read from stdin in
   reads of at most 64 bytes into a fixed buffer (a bounded reader: named in `tests/contract_bounded_readers.rs` if its
   census does not take the statement as bounded): `q` → `console-key{key:"quit"}`; byte 0x03 →
   `console-key{key:"interrupt"}`; both end the loop; any other read → one `console-key{key:"unbound"}` per read, never
   its bytes (architecture · decision/codes-only-role-logs). On the end: the restore, then
   `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:0}`, exit 0. Every write to the terminal goes through the human module's
   writer, never a print macro (the workspace lints). No board read, no channel frame, no compositor call. The loop
   and the guard take their input, their output and their terminal-mode handle as values, so a unit test drives them
   with an in-memory reader and writer and no terminal (a test double, no product seam: no env var, flag or feature).
   Two unit cases in `src/console/` prove the restore comes before anything the catch site prints:
   `console_run_on_a_failing_read_writes_the_restore_before_it_returns_the_error` — the reader fails on its first read:
   `run` returns `Err`, and the writer's bytes END with the restore sequence; and
   `console_run_panicking_in_the_loop_writes_the_restore_during_the_unwind` — the reader panics: inside the test's own
   `catch_unwind`, the writer's bytes end with the restore sequence by the time the unwind returns. With main.rs's frame
   (step 4: the print only after `catch_unwind` returns), these two cases are the proof of restore-then-print.

- cli: no interactive prompt, pager or redraw, and input is stdin / `--file` only, except the terminal fleet console (`viola console`), its own surface, which reads keys from stdin in raw mode and redraws on a resize; tui: once the child starts the terminal belongs to the child, and viola writes zero bytes of its own to it (only a start's automatic verify lines L1 to L5 and verify's own output precede the child's bytes, and only a not-resumed `viola adopt`'s refusal pair or document follows them once the child ends) (under `viola revive --json` or `viola adopt --json` a `pump_child` error prints no document: viola writes nothing past it, and a peer the wrapper refuses is dropped in `accept_loop`, before its worker thread and any frame: it writes nothing to the outer terminal and moves no wheel), and once the wrapped child holds the terminal, human keystrokes are never blocked, refused or dropped: queued with the paste in arrival order, they wait behind at most its in-flight chunk and closing marker (the one exception is a start's automatic verify window, before the child starts: a key typed then waits in the terminal's own buffer), and focus / mouse / resize sequences and terminal replies (F-W2's closed list) are never counted as editing; every other byte is. viola has no web or graphical frontend; the terminal fleet console's keyboard reach is the route entry «Fleet a11y verification»'s.

- CLI exit codes: 0 · 1 (a `cli` verb's internal error: `error: internal error` on stderr, or under `--json` before a `--` the catch site's `{"v":1,"error":"internal-error","detail":null}` on stdout, stderr then empty, `run`, `revive`'s start, `adopt`'s start, `mcp` and `hook` silent at that site; also `viola run`'s and `viola revive`'s start, and `viola verify`, refusing the home tree before any log opens: the home-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair, or the instance-state pair for an instance-level refusal, no line written, no child started; also `viola run`'s, `viola revive`'s and `viola adopt`'s start refusing the socket directory (`socket_dir_ready`, before any snapshot, child or `Server::bind`; a failed create and a refused check read this one code, a `Server::bind` failure does not): the stderr `unable:` / `hint:` pair, or under `viola revive --json` the `socket-dir-refused` document, and one `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"socket-dir-refused"}`, no path, pid or uid; `viola verify`'s refusals each carry their code on the `process-exit` it writes under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME`: `program-not-found` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `version-unreadable` · `strict-modes-failed` · `unclean-fixture` · `untrusted-folder` (a probe run's first screen read the trust or imports form; no stamp written), beside `interrupted`; a failing row is no refusal and carries no code, yet `viola verify` still exits 1 on a failed relied row with that row's stamp written, and `verify` takes no `--json`; also `viola open`'s refusals, `strict-modes-failed` before any log, `already-live`, `stale-heartbeat`, `pinned-hash-mismatch`, `terminal-not-found`, `not-live` or `internal-error`, each under `--json` the `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` document; also `viola adopt`'s refusals, under `--json` one refusal document whose `<code>` is one of `strict-modes-failed` · `session-live` · `not-resumed` · `already-live` · `stale-heartbeat` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `squatted-name` · `socket-dir-refused` · `internal-error` (`session-live` when a `claude agents --json` row carries the adopted id); also `viola focus`'s and `viola up`'s refusals, each an `unable:` / `hint:` pair on stderr with no path, or under `--json` one refusal document (`viola up`'s `boot-time-unread`, `strict-modes-failed`, `pinned-hash-mismatch` or `terminal-not-found`); also `viola console`'s refusals, each an `unable:` / `hint:` pair on stderr with no path; also a `viola up` whose lines are not all successes) · 2 (usage error, and `viola send` text over 16 MiB or not UTF-8) · 10 human-typing · 11 unassigned (the retired `budget-paused` refusal's code, never reused or renumbered) · 12 unverified-cli · 13 not-delivered · 14 unknown · 20 wrapper fault (a `-32602` from `link` / `unlink` included) · 21 instance unreachable (under `--json` `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"<cause>"}`, written by `client::unreachable_document` (the board builds its own), `<cause>` one of the six exit-21 words of `viola_core::UnreachableCause`'s closed seven (the seventh, `call-deadline`, written by the MCP frame tools alone) `strict-modes-failed` · `instance-dead` · `unwrapped-name` · `endpoint-lost` · `server-verify-failed` · `socket-dir-refused`, no `RefusalReason`; with no live endpoint `viola_state::liveness::without_endpoint` reads an instance directory as `instance-dead` and anything else as `unwrapped-name`, so a stale instance reads `instance-dead`, and a wrapper lost with the call open reads `endpoint-lost`; also, on `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` / `pause` / `release` / `link` / `unlink`, a server that is not the recorded wrapper — a connected peer whose euid is not this user's or cannot be read (`peer_admitted`), or the connected peer's pid or OS start time not the snapshot's, or that check not made — no frame written, `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"server-verify-failed"}` under `--json` (Linux only; the Windows and macOS legs left with their code, recoverable at the tag `multi-os-final`), after the client's own exit-13 refusals, the strict-modes instance check and the socket-directory check, with no exit code or `RefusalReason` of its own, its `--json` word the document's `detail`; also `viola list`'s refused strict-modes check of the home, `instances/` or any one instance, which refuses the whole board, no log opened, and `viola up`'s same board refusal (`instance-unreachable`, `strict-modes-failed`), with no line printed; also `viola focus`'s refused strict-modes check: the `unable:` / `hint:` pair, or `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"strict-modes-failed"}` under `--json` with stderr empty, nothing under the home opened and no line written; Both `viola revive` arms (the start arm and `--list`) and `viola adopt`'s start run their instance check before the log init as well: a refused check is the stderr pair, or under `--json` the `{"v":1,"error":"strict-modes-failed","detail":null}` document, and exit 1 with no log opened. `viola link` / `viola unlink` (on `instances/<driven>`) and `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `viola focus` and `viola switch` (on their named instance; `send` after its text read) run `check_instance` on the home and the instance through the one `client::refuse_untrusted` before the log init too: a refusal is exit 21, the fixed instance-state pair or under `--json` the `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"strict-modes-failed"}` document, with no role file opened and the directory's mode left as found. `viola console` runs its strict-modes check before the log init too: a refusal is exit 1 with the home pair, no line and the mode left as found. `viola run`, `viola revive`'s start arm and `viola adopt`'s start (after their instance check) run the home-tree check `strict::check_home_tree` (through `checked_exe`: the home, the `check_instance` set, `ledger/`, `bin/`, `plugin/`, `bin/<key>/`, the pinned copy, `plugin/<key>/` and its `hooks/` and `.claude-plugin/`, each that exists) before the wrapper log: a refusal is exit 1 with the home pair (the instance pair for an instance-level refusal; under `viola revive --json` or `viola adopt --json` the `strict-modes-failed` document), no log opened, no line and no child.

- `hook` → exit 0, empty stdout; `cli` → `process-exit{detail:"internal-error"}` when an instance resolves, then exit 1 with exactly `error: internal error` (no hint), or under `--json` (read from argv before any `--`) the `{"v":1,"error":"internal-error","detail":null}` document on stdout with stderr empty; `run` → `process-exit{detail:"internal-error"}` (the catch site prints nothing; under `viola revive --json` an anyhow error from `trusted`, `checked_exe`, `open_wrapper_log`, `preflight` or `start` prints the `internal-error` document before it returns, `pump_child`'s prints none); `mcp` main-thread → no `process-exit` line (`obs::internal_error_exit_line` covers `Run` and `Cli` only), then exit 1 with nothing on stdout; `console` → restores the terminal first, then `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"internal-error"}` in `console.ndjson`, `error: internal error` once on stderr and exit 1 (the catch site classes it as `cli`). Exit 21's `--json` document carries one cause word of `viola_core::UnreachableCause` in `detail`, written by the one `unreachable_document` (`src/cmd/client.rs`; `refuse_untrusted` and `src/cmd/plugin.rs` through it), and the type writes no log line of its own.
